title: fhevm sdk npm manifest
description: Inventory of every source package.json in the sdk/ discovery universe defined by fhevm-npm/npm-rules.md, plus repository-wide npm and toolchain policy.
$comment: This schema enforces manifest-local shape and kind invariants. A TypeScript validator must enforce filesystem, package.json and cross-entry invariants: complete discovery, key/path containment, member/workspaces equality, package names and privacy, required published package.json fields, private version 0.0.0, exports, dependency rules, dev/published ownership cardinality, and the conventional test:publint, test:consumer, conditional test:vendored and conditional test:mirror scripts.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, so editors validate the manifest as it is typed.

inventory.description: Filesystem scope controls for package.json inventory discovery.

exclude.description: Directory trees below sdk/ that are outside the fhevm-npm inventory scope.

forbidden.description: Package names forbidden from every dependency section unless the exact package entry declares an exception.

foundry.description: Repository-wide Foundry toolchain policy. This is the single source of truth; packages must not carry .foundry-version files.

version.description: Exact version reported by the first line of `forge --version`, without the `forge Version:` prefix.

packageJson.description: Required and excluded package.json fields, selected by manifest package kind.

packages.description: Every in-scope source package.json under sdk/, keyed by its directory relative to sdk/ — leading `./`, no trailing slash, and `.` for the workspace root itself.
packages.$comment: Keyed by relative path and not by package name, because a name is neither always present nor unique: five non-package manifests have no `name` at all, and v12/pkg and v13/pkg both publish as @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext. Relative paths are unique by construction, so the key doubles as the identity `publishedRelPath` points at. Non-members are included too: a standalone project and a non-package manifest are invisible to `workspaces` yet both change how resolution behaves.

packageJsonKindPolicy.description: Top-level package.json fields required or excluded for one package kind.

packageKey.description: The workspace root `.` or a path below it with leading `./`; `.` and `..` are forbidden as segments.

prefixedRelativePath.description: A non-empty relative path with leading `./`; `.` and `..` are forbidden as segments.

unprefixedRelativePath.description: A non-empty relative path without leading `./`; `.` and `..` are forbidden as segments.

filename.description: One filename, not a path; `.` and `..` are forbidden.

mirror.description: An independent Git repository kept synchronized with this package entry. Mirroring is an optional capability, not a package kind.

repository.description: Canonical HTTPS URL of the independent repository.

pinnedSource.title: Pinned external source
pinnedSource.description: A directory in another repository, frozen at one commit. Mirrors `fhevm.vendoredFrom` in the published package.json, so a gate can compare the two.
pinnedSource.$comment: `to` from that field is deliberately not repeated here: the destination is the element's own `relPath`, and one fact recorded twice is one fact that can disagree with itself.

repository.description: Clone URL of the repository the bytes came from.
repository.$comment: A pattern rather than `format: uri`, which needs an optional validator plug-in and is silently ignored without one.

tag.description: Release tag the copy was taken at. Human-readable, and the thing a reader compares against upstream.

commit.description: Full 40-character commit SHA the copy was taken at.
commit.$comment: Required alongside the tag because a tag can be moved and a commit cannot. The tag says which release was intended; the commit is what makes the copy reproducible.

from.description: Directory inside that repository, relative to its root. Written without a leading `./`, matching `fhevm.vendoredFrom.from` byte-for-byte.
from.$comment: The one relative path in this file with no `./`, so it stays comparable to the published field it mirrors. Do not normalise it.

vendoredElement.description: One directory of byte-for-byte copies: the whole directory when `files` is absent, otherwise only the files named.

relPath.description: Directory holding the copies, relative to this entry's own key and written with a leading `./`.

files.description: Filenames inside `relPath` that are copies. Omit to mean the whole directory is vendored.
files.$comment: Naming files rather than the directory keeps a vendored copy and hand-written code side by side in one directory, which is how sdk/common-vendored/src lands in pkg/ts/types today.

source.description: Where the bytes come from. A string when the source is a directory in this repository; an object when it is a pinned point in another repository.
source.$comment: Two shapes because there are two kinds of copy. A directory in this repository is always in step with the working tree, so a relative path is the whole answer. A copy from elsewhere is frozen at one commit, and without that commit nothing can tell a legitimate upstream change from drift in the copy.

oneOf.title: In-repository directory
oneOf.description: Relative path to the source directory, relative to the FHEVM REPO ROOT — not to sdk/ — with a leading `./`. Example: `./sdk/common-vendored/src`.
oneOf.$comment: Repo root rather than sdk/, because a vendored source is not always inside sdk/. Anchoring there avoids `../` segments that would read as though they could escape the checkout.

reason.description: Why the original cannot simply be imported. Prose, one sentence.
reason.$comment: Required, and the most important field here. A copy whose reason no longer holds is a copy to delete, and nothing else in the repository records why one was made.

kind.description: Which of the seven kinds in fhevm-npm/npm-rules.md § Definitions this directory is.
kind.$comment: A closed set on purpose. Left open, each gate invents its own vocabulary and the manifest stops being a single answer.

oneOf.description: The only kind that reaches npmjs.com. Not private, declares `exports`, and always sits in a `pkg/` subdirectory.
The member directory wrapping exactly one published package, holding its scripts, config and tests. Private, named `…-dev`.
Private code that several dev packages import, with no published counterpart of its own. Private, named `…-dev`.
A member that installs the published packages in order to test them, and ships nothing itself. Private, named `…-dev`.
A consumer deliberately left out of `workspaces`, keeping its own lockfile and running its own install.
An unnamed package.json that supplies directory-local metadata inside another package or project, without defining an independently installable package.
`sdk/` itself: the member list plus the toolchain every member shares. Private, never published, a member of nothing.

type.description: Module formats this package.json exposes or executes.

browser.description: Whether this package is designed and supported to run in a browser environment.

name.description: The package.json `name`. Absent only for a non-package manifest, which has no independent npm identity.

member.description: Whether the root package.json `workspaces` array lists this entry's key.
member.$comment: Duplicating `workspaces` deliberately: the gate that compares the two is what catches a member added in one place and forgotten in the other.

private.description: The package.json `private` field when relevant. Required true for dev packages, shared helpers, internal consumers and the workspace root; forbidden on published packages.

publishedRelPath.description: For kind `dev`: the directory of the published package this one wraps. Same form as a key in `packages` — relative to sdk/, leading `./` — always a subdirectory of this entry's own key, and always the key of another entry whose `kind` is `published`.
publishedRelPath.$comment: A relative path and not a package name, because a name is not unique here: v12/pkg and v13/pkg both publish as @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext, so only the relative path says which one. It must be written exactly as that entry's key, `./` included, since matching the two is how a reader follows the link. This is the relationship npm cannot express — a dev package and its published package share no field tying them together, only the directory nesting, and nesting is a convention rather than a guarantee.

dependencyGroup.description: The dependency-alignment group this package belongs to, as a relative path prefix. Omitted by anything that spans groups, such as a shared helper or the workspace root.
dependencyGroup.$comment: What makes the sibling-agreement rule checkable: siblings sharing a dependency group must declare identical ranges, while different groups are free to differ. It is a safe open path rather than an enum so adding a group does not require a schema or rule edit; the TypeScript validator checks that it is a prefix of the entry key.

dependencyExceptions.description: Forbidden dependency names exceptionally allowed in this exact package.json only.
dependencyExceptions.$comment: The TypeScript validator checks that each value is globally forbidden and actually declared by this package.

vendored.description: Directories or files inside this package that are byte-for-byte copies of something else, because importing the original is impossible. Omitted when the package vendors nothing.
vendored.$comment: Vendoring is a last resort, so every element states why importing was impossible. Listing copies here makes them reviewable: a reason that has stopped being true is the signal to delete the copy and import instead. The implementation of the check is deliberately not stored per element; the TypeScript validator requires one conventional test:vendored script on the test owner, and CI executes it.

note.description: Anything else a reader needs that no package.json field can hold. Prose, one sentence.

allOf.$comment: A published package is named and omits private entirely. Its member status remains variable because only one package generation carrying a shared published name may be a workspace member.

Every dev package, shared helper and internal consumer is a named private workspace member with the visible `-dev` suffix. The matching `version: 0.0.0` rule is checked in package.json by the TypeScript validator.
A dev package exists to wrap exactly one published package; recording which is the whole point of the entry.
Only a dev package owns a published package. Other kinds cannot carry publishedRelPath.
A non-package manifest is never a member, has no package name and carries no ownership, dependency-group or content-distribution metadata.
A standalone project is deliberately outside `workspaces` so it keeps its own lockfile.
The workspace root is the required `.` entry, is private, and is not a member of itself. It has no owner, dependency-group or content-distribution metadata.
